intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that annular epidermolytic ichthyosis-1 (AEI1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding keratin-10 (KRT10).

checks.claim: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis-1 (AEI1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the KRT10 gene, which encodes keratin-10.
checks.evidence_quote: Molecular analysis revealed a novel tandem CG to GA 2-bp mutation in the same allele of keratin 10 in affected individuals
checks.explanation: A mutation on one allele with autosomal dominant inheritance means the mutation is heterozygous in KRT10.

paragraphs.text: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is a rare phenotypic variant of epidermolytic ichthyosis (bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma). Affected individuals have bullous ichthyosis in early childhood and hyperkeratotic lichenified plaques in flexural areas and on extensor surfaces at later ages. They also have intermittent bouts of annular and polycyclic, erythematous, scaly plaques on the trunk and proximal extremities (Suga et al., 1998). Palmoplantar keratoderma can be present (Mikilita et al., 2020).

checks.claim: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is a rare phenotypic variant of epidermolytic ichthyosis (bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma).
checks.evidence_quote: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is a distinct phenotypic variant of bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma that has recently been described in two separate kindreds.
checks.explanation: The paper calls it a 'distinct' variant, not a 'rare' one, although only two prior kindreds suggests rarity. It also does not use the term 'epidermolytic ichthyosis' as a synonym.

checks.claim: Individuals with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis have bullous ichthyosis in early childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: Individuals with this variant present with bullous ichthyosis in early childhood

checks.evidence_quote: hyperkeratotic lichenified plaques in the flexural areas and extensor surfaces at later ages.

checks.evidence_quote: Characteristically, they also develop intermittent bouts of annular and polycyclic, erythematous, scaly plaques on the trunk and proximal extremities.

checks.evidence_quote: characterized by erythematous, polycyclic, and migratory scaly plaques accompanied by palmoplantar keratoderma
checks.explanation: Abstract describes palmoplantar keratoderma as a feature of AEI.

paragraphs.text: Sahn et al. (1992) reported a 30-year-old white woman who developed bullous and ichthyosiform skin lesions at the age of 8 months. Blistering stopped at puberty, but the hyperkeratotic plaques persisted. At age 27 years, she developed numerous pruritic annular and polycyclic, erythematous, hyperkeratotic plaques on the trunk and extremities that enlarged slowly and then resolved. Biopsy of the annular plaques showed epidermolytic hyperkeratosis, and electron microscopy showed interrupted perinuclear tonofilament rings. Two of her 5 children had a bullous type of ichthyosis.

checks.explanation: The paper is titled 'Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis: a unique phenotype,' and the abstract describes this woman's case.

paragraphs.text: Joh et al. (1997) reported a second family with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis, with 2 affected generations. The proband had bullous ichthyosis, with bouts of disease activity in which numerous annular and polycyclic erythematous, hyperkeratotic plaques developed on the trunk and proximal extremities. Histology showed epidermolytic hyperkeratosis, and ultrastructural study showed abnormal keratin filament networks and perinuclear clumping of tonofilaments.

paragraphs.text: Mikilita et al. (2020) reported an 8-year-old girl, with no family history of the disorder and no parental consanguinity, who had diffuse skin disease beginning in the first months of life. She had erythematous, scaly, hyperkeratotic plaques with prominent geographic borders on the mesogastrium, cubital and popliteal fossae, and inguinal and cervical regions, together with palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and yellowish hyperkeratotic plaques on the scalp and nasal introitus. Hair, nails, and mucosa were normal. When reexamined 1 month later, the plaques had changed in appearance, the affected area had expanded, and the polycyclic pattern had disappeared. A biopsy from the forearm showed acanthosis, papillomatosis, and hyperkeratosis with marked epidermolysis in the granular layer.

paragraphs.text: In their patient, Mikilita et al. (2020) first suspected erythrokeratodermia variabilis et progressiva. They made the diagnosis of annular epidermolytic ichthyosis after histopathology showed epidermolytic hyperkeratosis. They noted that erythrokeratodermia variabilis et progressiva differs in its onset during childhood, its lack of epidermal fragility, and its histology without epidermolysis.
